readings: Link each invoice line item to its order through its invoice (`Invoices.order_id`), and from the order to the customer's town or city. First, for each order item id and town, average the line `product_price` and the ratio `derived_product_cost` / `derived_total_cost`, ignoring missing values. Then, for each town, average those per-item averages. Show the towns whose average cost ratio is above the average of that ratio across all towns, with the town, its average price, its average ratio, and how much its ratio exceeds the cross-town average. No rounding.
queries:
WITH item_averages AS (
    SELECT
        ili.order_item_id,
        c.town_city,
        AVG(ili.product_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(CAST(ili.derived_product_cost AS REAL) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS average_ratio
    FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.invoice_number = ili.invoice_number
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
),
town_averages AS (
    SELECT
        town_city,
        AVG(average_price) AS average_price,
        AVG(average_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM item_averages
    GROUP BY town_city
),
cross_town_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_ratio) AS average_ratio
    FROM town_averages
)
SELECT
    t.town_city,
    t.average_price,
    t.average_ratio,
    t.average_ratio - a.average_ratio AS ratio_excess
FROM town_averages AS t
CROSS JOIN cross_town_average AS a
WHERE t.average_ratio > a.average_ratio;
